title: Editor tools & selection engine (part 1 of the C04 split) — bounded extraction packets
status: read-only census complete; no source mutated; proposed IDs and packet boundaries are placeholders for the orchestrator to renumber into the global P-sequence and fold into engineering/inventory/remediation-scope.json
coverage_note: All 4 in-scope files (13,281 lines total) are assigned to exactly one packet each below, split by line range where a file spans several unrelated responsibilities — mirroring how C05 split export.js and C04b split ui.js. tools.js (8,643 lines, ~65% of this census) -> 33 packets; select-bridge.js (3,627 lines) -> 14 packets; subselect-bridge.js (549 lines) -> 4 packets; symmetry-bridge.js (462 lines) -> 3 packets. This is C04a, the first half of the C04 split recorded on issue #1039 (C04b — ui.js, all editor *-panel.js, the remaining editor *-bridge.js, and the standalone drawing/text/rig/mesh/brush modules — is a separate, sibling census under Honey's own worktree/PR #1074, not read here). Read every line of all 4 files (no sampling). Confirmed zero file overlap with C04b's scope list (ui.js, *-panel.js, group-bridge.js, draw-bridge.js, shape-bridge.js, pen-bridge.js, eraser-bridge.js, fill-bridge.js, feedback-bridge.js, rig-widget.js, image-mesh-bridge.js, etc.), with C05/#1040's scope (native-video-bridge.js, psd-import-bridge.js, export.js, media-library.js, linked-media.js, the Rust files), and with C06/#1041's scope (src/js/labs/**) — none of those paths appear anywhere in this census's 4 files or vice versa. engine-bridge.js and updater-bridge.js are referenced throughout as external dependencies only (every tool bridge calls into engine-bridge.js for screenToWorld/suspend/resume/renderNow/isEnabled), matching the exclusion convention both C05 and C04b already established for that pair.

packets.title: Shared tool-agnostic globals and shift-constrain helpers
packets.responsibility: Module-level mutable state shared by every tool branch in this file (currentPath, selectedPaths, per-gesture flags) plus two small geometry helpers (45°/square shift-constrain) and the component-instance-under-a-point hit-test used by both the Select tool and Motion double-click.
packets.writer: sole in-memory owner of currentPath/selectedPaths/_moveDragStarted/_eraseDragActive/_compClick — none of these are persisted directly (selectedPaths is projected into state.selectedStrokeIndices for persistence elsewhere)
packets.public_api: none exported; plain top-level vars/functions consumed by every other packet in this file and by select-bridge.js/subselect-bridge.js (selectedPaths, hitTestComponentLayers)
packets.notes: selectedPaths/currentPath are the two most widely shared mutable globals in the whole editor-tools slice — any extraction has to either keep them as a shared module or convert every one of the ~40+ read/write sites across tools.js/select-bridge.js/subselect-bridge.js at once.

packets.title: Fill/Stroke Select — selection state, hit-test-at-point, promote-to-Select
packets.responsibility: Animate-style fill/stroke aspect selection: a drawn shape stays one Path, but this fakes independent fill-only/stroke-only/bounded-arc selection on top of it, plus promoting a virtual selection into real standalone Paths so the ordinary Select tool's transform box can take over. Registers 3 raw document-level pointerdown/move/up listeners (capture phase) for its own marquee/lasso drag and for promote-then-drag, independent of Paper.js's Tool event loop.
packets.writer: sole owner of module-private _fsSel; layer.insertChild for promoted clones (fsPromoteSelectionForTransform)
packets.public_api: none exported; consumed by tools.js's own onMouseDown/Up 'fsselect' branches and by the Fill/Stroke Select floating panel (labs-float-panel.js)
packets.notes: The 3 raw document.addEventListener(...,{capture:true}) registrations here run at module-load time, directly on `document`, not wrapped in any init()/IIFE — architecturally inconsistent with the convention every one of this census's 3 *-bridge.js files uses for their own DOM wiring (see cross_cutting_notes).

packets.title: Fill/Stroke Select — arc extraction, fill-region geometry, delete/break
packets.responsibility: The actual geometry behind Fill/Stroke Select: computing where a stroke crosses others (to bound a clicked arc), splitting a fill into two real regions across a crossing stroke's chord (open or closed cutter), the 'break at intersections' brush, and destructive delete/realize of a selected fragment.
packets.writer: layer.insertChild/remove for realized fragments; fsUnlinkFillRegen strips data.fillSeed*/fillWalls so a manually-touched fragment stops auto-regenerating
packets.public_api: fillVectorFind (cross-reference, called for the self-intersecting-fallback branch of fsFindFillRegion) — otherwise internal to the fsselect tool
packets.notes: fsFindFillRegion's closed-cutter branch and open-cutter branch are two independently-derived algorithms (boolean intersect/subtract vs. arc-join) for what is conceptually the same operation — kept separate per the function's own comment (Paper's boolean ops have no ambiguity for a closed cutter, the arc-join trick only works for an open one).

packets.title: Node/tangent edit (Subselect fallback) + vertex Position/Size/Rotation panel
packets.responsibility: Illustrator-style anchor/tangent-handle editing for the Subselect tool's Paper.js-native fallback, the vertex-scoped Position/Size/Rotation panel fields it feeds, vertex insertion (Alt+click on a curve), and dab/linkedFill-companion-to-anchor resolution shared with the fs-select and Select tools.
packets.writer: path.segments / path.data.centerSegments in place; nodeLayer.removeChildren()+add for the visual overlay
packets.public_api: resolveBrushAnchor, nodeEditTargetPath, nodeEditSegmentsData, renderNodeHandles, insertVertexAt — all consumed directly by select-bridge.js and subselect-bridge.js (same-name global functions, no module boundary between the three files today)
packets.notes: resolveBrushAnchor is the single choke point that redirects a click on a disposable brush-texture dab or linkedFill backdrop back to the real editable anchor — CLAUDE.md §1 pattern; re-implementing or forgetting it in a new click path silently lets the user 'select' a companion instead of the stroke it belongs to (this exact bug is cited twice in the file's own comments as already having happened once for dabs and once for linkedFill).

packets.title: Selection transform box: bounds, oriented (rotated) box, align/distribute
packets.responsibility: The 8-handle + rotate-ring transform box geometry for the Select tool's Paper.js-native fallback: computing a rotation-aware (not just axis-aligned) box from data.boxAngle, the 9-dot anchor-point convention, and the Align/Distribute toolbar actions (equal-gap spacing).
packets.writer: path.data.boxAngle/xformAnchorKey/xformAnchorCustom persisted per-stroke; xformLayer.removeChildren()+add for the overlay
packets.public_api: orientedSelBox, orientedBoxForPath, selBoxPt, xformAnchorPoint, XFORM_ANCHOR_PROP, scaleCenterSegments/rotateCenterSegments/shearCenterSegments — all consumed by select-bridge.js's own computeHandles()/hit-test/drag math, which explicitly recomputes from these rather than reading tools.js's own (now largely dead when the engine is on) xformHandles array
consumers: select-bridge.js (computeHandles, presetAnchorWorldPoints, every xform-* drag mode)
engine-bridge.js (buildTransformBoxItems, buildHoverBoxItems — mirrors this box math for the Rust-drawn overlay)
packets.notes: orientedSelBox/orientedBoxForPath/selBoxPt are duplicated in spirit (not verbatim) by engine-bridge.js's buildTransformBoxItems/buildHoverBoxItems, which must draw the identical box the Rust-mirror renders — a CLAUDE.md §3-style pair outside this census's own files.

packets.title: Selection lifecycle: clear/getSI, duplicate, canvas copy/cut/paste
packets.responsibility: serP/desP-based clone pipeline shared by ⌘D duplicate and canvas ⌘C/⌘X/⌘V — snapshots a stroke's brush-companion dabs and linkedFill backdrop (the two live-reference fields serP alone can't round-trip), rebuilds them with fresh ids, and remaps non-destructive combine-group membership so a copied group doesn't silently alias the source's group id.
packets.writer: layer.insertChild for materialized clones; ld.groups[freshId] for remapped combine groups
packets.public_api: _snapshotForClone/_materializeClones consumed directly by select-bridge.js's Alt+click-inside-selection duplicate-and-drag gesture
packets.notes: pasteSelection has its own held-frame promotion logic distinct from ensureKeyframe's blank/non-blank split (Motion mode writes into the hold's own inherited keyframe rather than promoting, so the pasted shape doesn't appear to vanish on scrub-back) — a third variant of the same held-frame problem CLAUDE.md's ensureKeyframe comment already documents two answers for.

packets.title: Stylus pressure capture (3 channels) + per-layer edit-refusal gate
packets.responsibility: Three independent stylus-pressure channels (raw Pointer Events, macOS webkitForce, Tauri native AppKit event) merged into one _stylus/_stylus.force reading; the single gate every drawing tool consults before mutating a layer (component/duplicator/pathFx/locked/nativeVideo/montage refusal reasons, each with its own toast); and ensureKeyframe, the sole promoter of a held frame into a real (blank-or-inherited) keyframe.
packets.writer: state.layers[i].frames[cur].isKeyframe/strokes via ensureKeyframe; no persisted state of its own otherwise
packets.public_api: window.canEditActiveLayer, window.editRefusalReason (exported); ensureKeyframe is a bare global called from nearly every commit path in tools.js/select-bridge.js/subselect-bridge.js and from draw-bridge.js/pen-bridge.js/shape-bridge.js/fill-bridge.js/eraser-bridge.js (outside this census)
consumers: every drawing/edit tool in this census and in C04b's draw-bridge.js/pen-bridge.js/shape-bridge.js/fill-bridge.js/eraser-bridge.js
packets.notes: ensureKeyframe's `blank` flag encodes a deliberate, non-obvious asymmetry (content-creating tools start the new keyframe empty; every edit tool needs the inherited content still there) — CLAUDE.md-worthy invariant that isn't itself in CLAUDE.md yet; a future new tool must pick the right side explicitly rather than copy whichever call site is nearest.

packets.title: Stroke identity, ownership tagging, and team-review fork/ghost lifecycle
packets.responsibility: ensureStrokeId (the stable per-stroke id every other system in this census keys off), Shadow Brush tagging, Mask-mode/ownership tagging on every drawn shape, and the full team-review fork-into-ghost / accept / reject lifecycle for editing or deleting a co-worker's stroke.
packets.writer: path.data.strokeId/ownerId/ownerName/ownerColor/revisionParentId/isRevisionGhost/revisionAction/preRevisionOpacity
packets.public_api: ensureStrokeId, tagOwner, forkIfForeignOwner, markDeleteAsRevision/accept/rejectDeleteRevision/acceptRevision/rejectRevision — all called from select-bridge.js/subselect-bridge.js's own commit paths, and (per DEF-2 below) NOT called from tools.js's own onMouseUp Select/Subselect commit paths
packets.notes: See DEF-2: tools.js's own mouse-drag transform/move/node-drag commit paths (onMouseUp) never call forkIfForeignOwner even though this exact file defines it and select-bridge.js/subselect-bridge.js call it on every one of their own equivalent commits with an explicit 'Team review' comment.

packets.title: Fill closing-line overlay, persistent invisible closing stroke, snap-to-wall
packets.responsibility: Alt+drag closing-stroke gesture (Harmony 'Close Gap' model): a transient in-progress dashed overlay, a queue of completed-but-not-yet-consumed closing strokes, and the persistent invisible (no real color) fillCloseLine Path that survives save/tween once committed, snapped onto nearby real ink so it doesn't drift off the line it's meant to bridge.
packets.writer: layer.addChild for a committed fillCommitCloseLine Path (data.isFillCloseLine, no strokeColor)
packets.public_api: fillCommitCloseLine, fillSnapWalls, fillBuildWallSnapper — consumed by fillPropagateAcrossFrames to re-anchor/re-emit closing lines per frame
consumers: engine-bridge.js's buildSceneJson (renders fillCloseStrokesOverlayItems as a dashed guide only while the Fill tool is active)
packets.notes: fillSnapWalls' own exclusion list (dabs, linkedFill companions, other closing lines) exists specifically to stop an O(points × dabs) slowdown a textured-preset stroke previously caused, plus a snap target landing on a stray dab edge instead of the real line.

packets.title: Automatic gap closure (extend / radius modes)
packets.responsibility: Blender Grease-Pencil-style automatic gap closing: 'extend' continues each open stroke end along its own tangent until it hits real ink; 'radius' bridges any two open ends within a distance — both transient, recomputed fresh from the frame's own strokes on every fill click, never persisted.
packets.writer: none persisted (emitted Paths are tagged isFillAutoClose and removed by the caller in the same synchronous handler)
packets.public_api: fillAutoCloseWalls — called once per fill click (tools.js) and once per propagated frame (fillPropagateAcrossFrames)
packets.notes: Deliberately stateless per the file's own comment: unlike the persistent closing line, nothing here needs anchor tracking across frames, which is exactly what makes it also 'fix propagation for free' (no drift across a tween span).

packets.title: Wall graph construction + sharpest-turn face tracing
packets.responsibility: Builds a graph over every candidate wall's endpoints (real stroke edges + synthetic gap edges within a threshold), with self-loop/coincident-duplicate/spur pruning, then traces the smallest enclosing face from a seed edge by always taking the sharpest available turn — the pure-JS peer of geometry-wasm's fill.rs build_graph/trace_loop, hand-kept in sync (CLAUDE.md §3).
packets.writer: none (pure query, operates on disposable clone Paths)
packets.public_api: internal to fillVectorFindJS only
packets.notes: Every pruning/dedup fix here (self-loop guard, coincident-duplicate guard, spur pruning) is explicitly cross-referenced in-comment as 'kept in sync with build_graph/fill.rs' — a change to one side without the other silently reintroduces a bug the other side already fixed.

packets.title: Fill z-order insertion, recolor-in-place matching, same-color merge
packets.responsibility: Where a new fill lands in the layer's stacking order (just above whatever it visually covers), detecting a paint-bucket click that just re-traces an existing shape's own outline (recolor instead of stacking a duplicate), and Animate-style same-color fill fusion — guarded against unioning two near-identical polygons (numerically unsafe in Paper's clipper) and against silently erasing a hand-drawn divider between two same-colored regions.
packets.writer: layer.insertChild/remove; merges tag the survivor with a merged data.fillSeeds array (see C04a.fill.regenerate-linked)
packets.public_api: fillMergeSameColor — called by both the paint-bucket click handler and the Fill Brush commit path (draw-bridge.js, outside this census) with a different allowFillShapeAbsorb argument
consumers: C04a.fill.match-merge's own booleanOp() caller for the 'merge' Fill Brush placement mode
packets.notes: _isNearIdenticalArea's bounds+area proxy exists specifically to short-circuit BEFORE ever calling .unite() on two near-duplicate polygons — a real, previously-hit numerical-safety issue (23 garbage fragments from unioning a shape with its own clone), not a style preference.

packets.title: Multi-seed and single-seed fill regeneration on wall edit
packets.responsibility: Re-traces every fill bucket in a layer whose bounding strokes just moved — wall-restricted (data.fillWalls) fills skip a full re-trace of unrelated fills entirely (a perf fix for the eraser's per-pointermove call rate); a merged/'collé' fill independently re-traces and re-unions every one of its stored seeds rather than collapsing to one.
packets.writer: layer.insertChild/remove on the fill Path; rewrites its data.fillSeed(s)/fillGapPx/fillWalls to the freshly-resolved geometry
packets.public_api: fillRegenerateLinked — called from nearly every geometry-editing commit path across this census (node-drag, transform-box commit, boolean ops, eraser) plus draw-bridge.js/eraser-bridge.js outside it
packets.notes: The onlyIds wall-restriction (not a distance cap) is the actual safety guarantee against a regenerated fill grabbing unrelated artwork, no matter how far its own bounding strokes move — the gap-cap alone is a legacy fallback only for fills that predate this association.

packets.title: Fill propagation across frames (Auto-Paint)
packets.responsibility: Re-traces a bucket fill on every OTHER frame of the layer that owns its own strokes (skipping held frames on purpose), anchoring the seed relative to nearby walls' own local (tangent,normal) frames rather than an absolute click point, with two-stage wall-identity resolution (direct strokeId match, falling back to the tween autoMatch matcher) and a quality gate that leaves a frame untouched rather than write a visibly-wrong fill.
packets.writer: per-frame layer.insertChild/remove of the propagated fill + its closing lines; saveActiveLayerFrame() per frame
packets.public_api: fillPropagateAcrossFrames, describePropagateResult — called from the Tool Options button (fill-bridge.js, outside this census) and the frame right-click menu (timeline.js)
packets.notes: The quality gate (one FILL_GAP_STEPS tier of slack above the source's own closure quality) is a deliberately empirical fix for a measured mid-tween-span failure mode (a 12px gap's rebuilt bridge stretching to 309px by frame 15) — not a stylistic choice, a correctness fix for a reported regression.

packets.title: Fill-find dispatch: WASM primary, JS graph fallback, raster last resort
packets.responsibility: The paint bucket's core click-to-region solver: escalates through FILL_GAP_STEPS gap thresholds trying WASM's fill_find (geometry-wasm/src/fill.rs) first, JS's own graph tracer (C04a.fill.graph-tracer) only when WASM is genuinely unavailable/threw, and a from-scratch pixel flood-fill + boundary-trace as a final fallback immune to the whole class of graph-topology bugs (near-tangent self-crossings, wrong-pairing gap bridges) the vector approach keeps hitting.
packets.writer: none (pure query returning a disposable Path)
packets.public_api: fillVectorFind — the single entry point every other fill packet in this census calls
entangled_with: geometry-wasm/src/fill.rs (outside this census — CLAUDE.md §3 JS/Rust duplicate pair)
packets.notes: See DEF-1: FILL_MIN_AREA's own comment explicitly documents a known, NOT-yet-root-caused defect (a confirmed live -95px² degenerate sliver that the 4px² noise floor doesn't catch, since 95 > 4) — self-admitted as unresolved, not something this census is inventing.

packets.title: Stroke-style dash + generic variable-width outline sweep engine
packets.responsibility: Shared by Taper-ends and the pressure-simulated vector brush: sweeps a filled outline around a centerline given a per-sample width, with true 3-point-arc round caps, an open-stroke sweep and a dedicated closed-ring (boolean-subtract-derived annulus) variant for a loop gesture, and post-hoc self-intersection cleanup via Paper's own resolveCrossings+reorient — deliberately NOT a naive perpendicular offset (which folds back on itself on a tight loop).
packets.writer: none (returns a disposable outline Path; callers assign it to path.segments)
packets.public_api: buildVariableWidthPath — the single geometry engine every brush/taper/eraser-expansion consumer in this census calls
consumers: engine.rs's add_semicircle_cap (Rust twin for live preview, outside this census)
entangled_with: engine.rs (Rust live-preview cap construction, CLAUDE.md §3 parity note)
packets.notes: _findRingRevisit/_unsliceRingPath exist to reverse buildClosedRingOutline's own zero-width-seam merge on demand (needed by boolean ops fed a closed vector-brush ring) — a read-only, tolerance-tuned detector distinct from _eraseDegenerateSelfLoops' similar-looking but differently-tolerant revisit detection elsewhere in this file.

packets.title: Procedural brush presets table, tip-shape geometry, custom-stamp capture
packets.responsibility: The ~25-entry built-in preset table (chalk/charcoal/pencil/marker/ink/pastel/airbrush families) plus every per-dab geometry primitive: 6 tip shapes (ellipse/rect/polygon/splatter/custom-captured/bristle-scribble handled in the stamping loop itself), a seeded RNG for reproducible re-stamping across tween frames, cross-width placement distributions ported from rnote, and a slow low-frequency trajectory wobble (roughenPath) evaluated analytically to avoid a resampled-Path drift bug.
packets.writer: none (pure geometry factories)
packets.public_api: resolveBrushPreset, buildDabShape, captureBrushStamp (window.captureBrushStamp) — consumed by brush-preset-picker.js/brush-editor.js's live preview (outside this census) via the same functions this file's own applyBrushTexture uses
packets.notes: roughenPath's own header comment documents a previously-shipped, now-fixed bug: an earlier version built a fixed-resolution resampled+smoothed Path per live-drag rebuild, which measurably drifted (~2.4px) under the identical already-drawn prefix on every rebuild even with a fixed seed — replaced by a stateless analytic wrapper exposing only length/getPointAt/getTangentAt.

packets.title: buildBrushDabs — the dab-placement walk
packets.responsibility: Walks a path (or a roughened wrapper of one) at arc-length intervals, computing local width/spacing/rotation/scatter/opacity/value-jitter per stamp position from the preset + optional pressure widthProfile, branching into 3 structurally different per-position emission strategies (scribble woven marks, bristle parallel strands, default single-or-soft-edge-layered dab) plus a fixed marker-buildup pass at both ends for flat/rect tips — capped at BRUSH_MAX_DABS with a natural-density-preserving spacing-floor compression rather than the old length-only floor that thinned long strokes.
packets.writer: none (returns an array of disposable, unstyled dab Paths)
packets.public_api: buildBrushDabs — called only from applyBrushTexture (this census) and brush-preset-picker.js's live preview (outside it)
packets.notes: The cap-safety spacing-floor fix is measured and dated in-comment (chalk-blunt at 8px brush started compressing at ~2570px of accumulated length under the old 450-dab/length-only floor; doubling the cap to 900 pushes that to ~5150px while keeping worst-case commit cost at ~14.8ms, still inside the CLAUDE.md §5 perf envelope) — a genuine, already-resolved perf/quality tradeoff record, not a hypothetical.

packets.title: Brush-texture application, re-application, and Fill Brush placement modes
packets.responsibility: Turns a committed stroke into an invisible (or stroke-camouflaged, if it also has a fill) anchor plus a set of real dab Paths tagged with a shared data.brushGroupId; re-stamps on a subselect edit (drag-end only, not per mousemove); tears down and reapplies a different preset in place; and resolves the Fill Brush's Above/Below/Merge placement, including the boolean-merge branch that reuses insertBooleanResult.
packets.writer: basePath.data.brushCompanions/brushTexturePreset/brushGroupId/preTextureOpacity/preTextureStroke; layer.insertChild for dab Paths and the merge result's islands
packets.public_api: applyBrushTexture, regenerateBrushTexture, applyOrChangeBrushTexture — called from tools.js's own draw/pen/fillbrush commit branches, from subselect-bridge.js/select-bridge.js's node/transform commit tails, and from timeline.js's 'Apply to selection' menu
entangled_with: app.js (relinkBrushCompanions rebuilds the live data.brushCompanions array after every layer reload, per CLAUDE.md §1's live-reference rule)
packets.notes: The two invisible-anchor camouflage modes (opacity:0 for a stroke-only anchor vs. strokeColor:null only for a fill-carrying one) are exactly the pattern CLAUDE.md §1 calls out by name, including the '#ffffff fallback' pitfall these anchors are explicitly exempted from.

packets.title: Taper-to-floor-width helpers
packets.responsibility: Blends a raw per-sample width toward a small absolute floor (not a percentage of the local width) at both ends of a stroke, fixing a reported asymmetry where a mouse's natural end-of-gesture deceleration inflated the pressure-heuristic width right where the taper needed to shrink it most.
packets.writer: none (pure array transforms)
packets.public_api: taperWidthAtFrac used directly by finalizePen and applyStrokeProfileToPath's 'taper-both' kind
packets.notes: None beyond the header comment's own rationale — a small, self-contained, already-fixed asymmetry.

packets.title: Centerline construction from raw pressure samples
packets.responsibility: Keeps a dense, arc-length-indexed width profile independent of however aggressively Paper's simplify() reduces the editable centerline's own anchor count — fixing a reported bug where a fairly straight pressure stroke simplified to 2-3 anchors and lost nearly its whole pressure curve, reading as calligraphy (width-follows-angle) instead of a round brush (width-follows-pressure).
packets.writer: none (returns plain centerSegments arrays, callers assign to path.data.centerSegments)
packets.public_api: buildWidthProfile, widthAtFrac, simplifyIfNeeded — all reused by C04a.brush.stroke-profiles and C04a.brush.texture-apply-placement
packets.notes: simplifyIfNeeded's whole reason to exist is a Paper.js footgun: Path#simplify(0) silently falls back to the DEFAULT tolerance (2.5) rather than truly no-op, since the internal check is `t||2.5` — every call site forwarding a user 'Smooth' slider must skip the call entirely at 0, not pass 0 through. Re-verify any future new caller of path.simplify(...) against this same footgun.

packets.title: Stroke profiles (taper-in/out/both, bulge, even) — Sander van Dijk 6.2/6.3
packets.responsibility: Converts an existing plain stroke into the centerline+widthProfile pressure-brush representation in place (identity preserved — strokeId/groupId/channelTag/ownerId survive untouched), which is also what makes 6.3's along-the-stroke gradients free once the stroke is a filled ribbon; re-profiles an already-converted stroke via its own dense widthProfile rather than re-deriving from now-baked outline segments.
packets.writer: path.data.centerSegments/widthProfile/isVectorBrush/profileBase/strokeProfile; path.fillColor/strokeColor swap
packets.public_api: applyStrokeProfileToPath (window.SM.applyStrokeProfile wraps it, outside this census) — invoked from select-bridge.js's context menu (Convert to Fill + 5 profile shapes)
packets.notes: The dense-profile requirement (not just per-anchor widths) is load-bearing on a 2-anchor straight Line-tool stroke specifically — a per-anchor-only taper-both on 2 points would set BOTH ends to the floor width and linear-interpolate a hairline for the whole stroke, measured and fixed in-comment.

packets.title: Trim stroke ends + the vector-brush outline rebuild choke point
packets.responsibility: Blender-style trim of a short post-junction overshoot (capped by maxOvershoot, working on the centerline never the ribbon outline) to stop the fill engine's smallest-area-wins rule from preferring a tiny parasitic sliver; and rebuildVectorBrushOutline, the single choke point every centerline edit (node drag, scale, rotate, tween-generated frame) funnels through to re-derive the visible ribbon and keep a linked Fill Brush backdrop in sync.
packets.writer: path.segments/data.centerSegments/data.widthProfile in place; syncs path.data.linkedFill's own segments
packets.public_api: rebuildVectorBrushOutline — called from essentially every centerline-touching commit path in this census (node-tangent-edit, select-bridge.js, subselect-bridge.js) plus tweens.js's dabRecordsForTween (outside this census)
packets.notes: The linked-fill sync living inside this one choke point (rather than at each of its ~10+ call sites) is precisely why a Fill Brush backdrop never desyncs from its ribbon on any edit that reaches here — a genuinely good single-source-of-truth pattern, called out approvingly in its own header comment.

packets.title: Corner / smooth / symmetric point-type conversion
packets.responsibility: Illustrator-style anchor-type toggle for the selected Subselect vertices, abstracted over the plain-Path-segments vs. vector-brush-centerSegments representational split via 6 tiny accessor shims.
packets.writer: path.segments or path.data.centerSegments handle values
packets.public_api: setPointType — bound to the Properties panel's corner/smooth/symmetric buttons (timeline.js)
packets.notes: None — small, self-contained, no observed defects.

packets.title: Pressure-simulated vector brush (Paper-native fallback) + calligraphic nib
packets.responsibility: The engine-off fallback pressure pipeline: a One Euro filter (must stay numerically identical to draw-bridge.js's own copy per CLAUDE.md §3), 3-channel pressure sampling with pen-lift-hold logic, the rnote-ported pressure response curve, and a fixed-angle calligraphic-nib width multiplier layered on top of pressure.
packets.writer: none (writes into currentPath.segments via vbRebuildPreview only)
packets.public_api: vbPressureOf, applyPressureCurve (window.applyPressureCurve), vbWidthFor, brushAngleWidths — consumed by C04a.tools.core-pointer-dispatch's own draw/fillbrush branches
entangled_with: draw-bridge.js's own copy of the identical One Euro filter and pressure-curve logic (CLAUDE.md §3 duplicate pair, outside this census)
packets.notes: Every tuning constant here is explicitly commented 'MUST match draw-bridge.js's own copy exactly' — a textbook CLAUDE.md §3 hand-synchronized pair; changing one without the other changes how a stroke feels only when the engine happens to be off, which is easy to never notice in testing (same class of risk as DEF-2/DEF-3).

packets.title: Pen tool finalize (bezier anchor placement commit)
packets.responsibility: Closes/commits a Pen-tool path on double-click or click-near-start, including the Taper-ends conversion into a centerline ribbon and the Symmetry-guide/Shadow-brush/ownership tagging every other commit path also applies.
packets.writer: layer content via saveActiveLayerFrame()
packets.public_api: finalizePen — called from tools.js's own onMouseDown 'pen' branch (double-click detection) and onMouseMoveTool's preview-line drawing

packets.title: Boolean path operations (union/subtract/intersect/exclude) + WASM bridge

cross_cutting_notes: Three independent, explicitly self-documented 'line-for-line port' implementations of overlapping Select/Subselect gesture logic coexist across this census's own 4 files: tools.js's onMouseDown/onMouseDrag/onMouseUp 'select'/'subselect' branches (the Paper.js/engine-off fallback) versus select-bridge.js's onDown/onMove/onUp and subselect-bridge.js's onDown/onMove/onUp (the engine-accelerated primary path) — each bridge file's own header comment states outright that it is 'a faithful line-for-line port of the ... branches ... in tools.js'. This is CLAUDE.md §3's 'two implementations must be kept in sync by hand' duplication hazard playing out across whole files rather than a matched pair of functions, and it has already visibly drifted: DEF-2, DEF-3 and DEF-4 below are concrete, code-verified instances of features or safety checks that exist only on one side.

Team-review collaboration safety (forkIfForeignOwner, tools.js:2048) is defined once but invoked inconsistently: select-bridge.js's onUp and subselect-bridge.js's onUp both call it on every real geometry-changing commit with an explicit 'Team review' comment, while tools.js's OWN onMouseUp commit branches for the exact same gestures (Select transform/move, Subselect node-drag) never call it at all (DEF-2). Because CLAUDE.md §4 records that the Rust engine is OFF by default in a fresh preview tab until `await SMEngineBridge.setEnabled(true)` resolves, this gap sits in the code path that actually runs first in a fresh session — a scenario CLAUDE.md itself flags as easy to test against without ever awaiting the engine and therefore easy to never notice.

Several data.* tags introduced within this census's 4 files in 2026-08/09 (data.paramShape, data.trackRoleId/attachedToRoleId/attachOffset, data.tweenOn) have real read/write logic here, but their full CLAUDE.md §1 consumer checklist (buildSceneJson, saveActiveLayerFrame/saveAllLayerFrames, serP/desP, tween matching, export.js) lives in app.js/engine-bridge.js/tweens.js/export.js — all outside this census's 4-file scope — and was not independently re-verified against each of those consumers here. Recommended follow-up for the orchestrator's cross-file audit pass, not re-litigated in this read-only census.

getSI(path) (tools.js:1487) is an O(active-layer-child-count) linear scan, invoked via `.map(getSI)` at dozens of call sites across tools.js and select-bridge.js after nearly every selection-mutating gesture (duplicate, paste, marquee finalize, every transform-box commit). Not measured here, and therefore not filed as a defect, but the exact shape of hotspot CLAUDE.md §5bis/§5ter document as non-obvious until profiled at real scale (2000+ item scenes) — worth a profiling pass before assuming it is free.

insertBooleanResult (tools.js:6967), the CLAUDE.md-mandated single chokepoint for inserting any boolean/erase result, sits physically isolated ~285 lines after its own direct dependencies (flattenBooleanResult/carryBooleanData, tools.js:6273-6549), separated by the entire unrelated Dynamic Shapes section. A pure source-navigation hazard, not a runtime bug — flagged because a future edit to the boolean/erase/insert pipeline is easy to make in only one of the two locations without noticing the other exists.

tools.js registers several raw `document.addEventListener('pointerdown'/'pointermove'/'pointerup', ..., {capture:true})` listeners for the Fill/Stroke Select tool's own marquee/lasso and its break-brush gesture directly at module-load time (lines 128-452), mixed into an otherwise plain global-function/global-var file. This is architecturally inconsistent with the IIFE + explicit init()-on-DOMContentLoaded convention every other file in this census (select-bridge.js, subselect-bridge.js, symmetry-bridge.js) uses for its own DOM wiring — worth normalizing if this area is ever extracted into its own module boundary.

known_defects.summary: FILL_MIN_AREA's own comment self-documents a confirmed-live, NOT-yet-root-caused defect: a click near a small closed detail can produce a real but nearly-invisible -95px² fill (the smallest-area-wins comparison has no lower bound below the noise floor), which the 4px² FILL_MIN_AREA floor does not catch since 95 > 4. The comment states the true root cause (likely in how build_graph/fill.rs represents a near-tangent self-crossing) was not found as of this commit.
known_defects.severity: known limitation (self-documented in source, root cause not yet found)

known_defects.summary: tools.js's own onMouseUp 'select' commit branches (_xform.active and the plain 'move' branch) and its onMouseUp 'subselect' node-drag commit never call forkIfForeignOwner, unlike select-bridge.js's onUp (line ~2613/2704/2870) and subselect-bridge.js's onUp (line ~523), which call it on every equivalent real-edit commit with an explicit 'Team review' comment. With the Rust engine off (the default in a fresh preview tab per CLAUDE.md §4), dragging/scaling/rotating a co-worker's stroke via Select/Subselect silently edits it in place instead of forking a ghost + a new owned revision.
known_defects.severity: product-debt (collaboration-safety regression in the engine-off fallback path)

known_defects.summary: tools.js's onMouseDown/onMouseDrag 'select' and 'subselect' branches hit-test and drag using the raw pointer point directly against layer.hitTest/nodeHandles[].pos, never undoing a layer's Motion transform, a Component's symMatrix, or a shape's per-element Motion (elementMotionAt) the way select-bridge.js's onDown (hitPt/posedHit, layerMotionPointMap) and subselect-bridge.js's toLocalPoint explicitly do — each of the latter two citing a confirmed-live reproduction of exactly this class of bug for itself, now fixed there but never ported back to this fallback. Reachable in plain Animation 2D (not just Motion mode), since CLAUDE.md §8 confirms a layer's motionMat renders in either mode.
known_defects.severity: product-debt (engine-off fallback correctness gap, code-verified by direct comparison, not runtime-tested)

known_defects.summary: select-bridge.js has accumulated substantial Select-tool functionality with no Paper.js-fallback equivalent anywhere in tools.js's onMouseDown/Drag/Up 'select' branch: Ctrl-drag corner-pin distort, edge skew, Shift-axis-lock move, smart alignment guides, Alt-click-inside-selection duplicate-and-drag, the multi-layer selection box, native-video/null-layer transform handles+drag, tracked-role attach/suggestion menu items, and canvas-drag handles for dynamic-shape corner-radius/ellipse-arc/star-inner-ratio (PARAM_HANDLE_KINDS). A user with the Rust engine off has none of these on the Select tool.
known_defects.severity: product-debt / known-limitation (parity gap, not documented anywhere as an intentional engine-off scope cut)

known_defects.summary: The scale/rotate/skew handle-grab branch of onDown (`if(hh){...ensureKeyframe();selectedPaths=state.selectedStrokeIndices.map(...)...var h=computeHandles();`) re-hydrates selectedPaths purely from state.selectedStrokeIndices after ensureKeyframe()'s object rebuild, with no restore path for a cross-layer selection (which the sibling 'marquee' finalize branch, ~600 lines away, deliberately leaves as an empty index array per its own comment, since a cross-layer selection has no single per-layer index list to report) and no null-check on the computeHandles() result that immediately follows — unlike beginDistort (line 747), a few lines above in the same file, which does check `if (!h) return false;` before touching h.gCorners/h.bounds. A multi-shape marquee spanning per-shape layers inside an entered Component, followed by a handle-grab (not a body-drag) on the resulting box, is a plausible reproduction of a null-pointer crash on h.bounds/h.gCorners. Found via static code comparison across two nearby branches of the same function; not reproduced by running the app.
